summary: Perspective-diverse adversarial verification of the revised knee-edge OOD draft protocol, skeptic re-check of findings, completeness critic
logs: 4 lenses reviewed; 25 high/medium findings survived the skeptic

packed.verdict: The physics is correct. The stall identity, the T(a0) formula, the float32 edge values, the bit-identical thrust below the knee, the action-independent load, and every quoted share, anchor, removal rate and density all reproduce, by direct arithmetic on canonical code or by Monte Carlo over the reset law alone (no dynamics were simulated). The weaknesses are in what the layers claim to establish. (1) L3a is not enforced by any rule. K1b reduces to the true world gap rho for any critic that behaves the same in both worlds, so it repeats L2. K1a has no absolute floor, because V0(b) bounds RANDOM's KC only from above. As written, a CUTOFF critic that does not over-value the region at all can pass K1. (2) The restated L2.2 still overclaims. An unordered transition set from this deterministic simulator can be put back in order by exact next_obs-to-obs matching, and the two worlds' retained state distributions differ. What is actually true is narrower: the per-tuple law on the support is identical, and TD3+BC's losses never link tuples. (3) The "exact" L2 checks cannot detect errors in the quantities that matter. The identity residual cancels the state, horizon, gamma and continuation. The known-answer test covers only old probes at |a0| <= 0.5 and stall_slope 1.5. (4) The "action shift, not state shift" framing is tested only at start states and recorder anchors, never at the policy-visited states where K2 and K3 are scored. E2 is a subpopulation of the collection law, not the whole law. (5) The hull argument and the "near-OOD" label are imprecise. The condition is better described as an action-support violation of the censored dataset, a support-mismatch covariate shift; the hull and near-OOD language does not fit it. The coherence note's arithmetic is right as far as it goes. It shows K1a is reachable only for an ideal smooth extrapolator, with zero margin when KC_0.05(RANDOM) = +0.25. The draft is sound on physics but needs these fixes to L3 rules and to its OOD claims before it is frozen.

low_findings.section: Part 2 L2 PASS items 5-6; step 0.4 KILL 5-6
low_findings.claim: The draft gives no precedence between FAIL (KILL 5) and INCONCLUSIVE (KILL 6) when both trigger. Taking the minimum over predictors lets one bad predictor (for example, cubic extrapolation) produce a shelving FAIL. Using the same minimum for the sign control (item 6, rho_hat(+0.90) < 0) makes that test easier to pass.
low_findings.evidence: rho_hat = min_k[P_k - Q_stall] (line 104). Item 5 says a miss is INCONCLUSIVE (line 115), but KILL 5 (line 389) declares FAIL and shelving if items 1-4 or 6 miss, with no rule for when item 5 also misses. Minimizing helps the ≥ tests be conservative but pushes the '< 0' test toward passing.
low_findings.fix: State that a predictor-validity miss takes precedence (INCONCLUSIVE) over FAIL. Compute items 1-4 only on anchors where all predictors are valid. Use max_k (or the true rho) for the sign control.

low_findings.claim: The specified draw order for the reset mixture ('mixture uniform first, then current, wave and kick' from a named stream) conflicts with the canonical start draw, and options['start'] cannot carry drawn values.
low_findings.evidence: draw_starts (thrusterchain.py) draws floats (kick × N(0, I10)) first, then current, amplitude and phase, from env.np_random. start_law only accepts range overrides for current, wave and kick. Drawing current, wave and kick values from a separate stream would therefore need options['state'], which requires |s| ≤ 100 and resets t to 0.
low_findings.fix: Specify that the named stream draws only the mixture uniform. options['start'] then sets current = (0.1, 0.7) or (0.9, 1.1), and the environment draws floats, current, amplitude and phase in canonical order. Test this lineage replay bit for bit.

low_findings.claim: The OOD taxonomy is borrowed loosely. 'Near-OOD' is an OOD-detection term for semantic closeness; this condition is a support-mismatch covariate shift on (s, a) with no semantic shift. In BCQ/BEAR terms, W is outside the censored dataset's support but inside the recorder's support, and the logged log-density misstates the behavior law of CUTOFF's data.
low_findings.evidence: The recorder density is positive on W (0.98/0.2 + 0.01 at high load, 0.5 at low load; Part 3.3), and 'each row logs its exact log-density' of the uncensored law. CUTOFF's retained-data behavior law is the truncated density (renormalized by 0.506 at high load and 0.8 at low load, zero on W). The draft never relates its framing to BCQ's extrapolation error or BEAR's support constraint.
low_findings.fix: Frame the condition as 'dataset-support (censoring) action shift: extrapolation along a0 outside the empirical support, a covariate shift with support mismatch; the Bellman law on the support is unchanged'. Log, or document, the censored density for CUTOFF streams.

verified.section: Part 2 L3a; Part 5 Stage 1 K1a, K1b, V0(b), K3; coherence note
verified.claim: L3a says the critic over-values the region, but no rule requires it. K1b reduces to the true world gap rho and passes for any critic that is the same in both worlds. K1a has no absolute floor, because V0(b) bounds KC_0.05(RANDOM) only from above. K3's stall-world Δclip > 0 also follows largely from L2 once K2 holds.
verified.evidence: From the definition (DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:423), KC(C,stall) - KC(C,no-stall) = [critic slope difference across worlds] + {[Qn(-(K+d)) - Qn(-K)] - [Qs(-(K+d)) - Qs(-K)]}. Qs(-K) = Qn(-K) by L2.2, so the second term is the true rho(d). Critics trained on the same supported law therefore give K1b ≈ rho(0.10), whatever their sign of extrapolation. Example: a pessimistic critic with KC_no-stall = -0.6 and KC_stall = +0.2 gives K1b = 0.8, a pass. L2 item 2 already requires median rho_hat ≥ 0.75 (line 112). For K1a (line 442), V0(b) (line 436) caps median KC_0.05(RANDOM) at +0.25 with no lower bound. KC_R = -0.6 and KC_C = -0.1 pass K1a with a CUTOFF critic that does not over-value. For K3: by the identity, clipping a W- action to -KNEE raises thrust from T(a0) in [-0.8,-0.2] to -0.8 and lowers the cost term, so Δclip(stall) > 0 is nearly implied by entry (K2) together with L2 item 4.
verified.fix: Add an absolute critic rule: median KC_0.10(CUTOFF, stall) ≥ +0.5, and ≥ 0.5 × median rho_hat(-0.90) at the same anchors. Make V0(b) two-sided: |median KC_0.05(RANDOM)| ≤ 0.25. Relabel K1b as a non-identifiability consistency check, not as evidence of over-valuation. State that K3 measures the cost of entry, not that critic error caused it.

check.reason: The K1 sub-claims hold. K1b is approximately the true world gap rho(0.10) plus the difference between the two worlds' critic slopes, so two equally pessimistic critics pass it. V0(b) (DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:436) is one-sided, so K1a (line 442) passes with KC_R = -0.6 and KC_C = -0.1. In that case the failure reading at line 466 and the reading 'K1 passes and K2 fails: the BC anchor contains the over-valuation' (line 466) would be wrong, because there is no over-valuation to contain. The finding is overstated in two ways. First, a PASS also needs K2 (line 444), and entry into R_deep- against the BC pull toward -0.7263 needs lambda*(Q1(-0.9) - Q1(-0.726)) > about 0.03. With lambda of about 0.025, that is a Q1 gap above about 1.2 where the true gap is negative, so over-valuation at visited states is effectively required. Second, the K3 sub-claim is not a defect. L3c (line 129) claims only that going past the knee costs return, and line 467 already treats 'K2 passes, Δclip fails' as a contradiction of step 0.4. Medium, not high.
check.evidence: KC_d is defined at line 423. With Qs(-K) = Qn(-K) when the continuation stays within the knee, KC(C,stall) - KC(C,no-stall) = [Q1s - Q1n slope difference] + Qn(-(K+d)) - Qs(-(K+d)) = slope difference + rho(d). V0(b) at line 436 has only the bound <= +0.25. K2 at line 444. The failure readings at lines 465-466. The K3 contradiction clause at line 467. Stall thrust at slope 3: T(-0.9) = -0.50000005 and T(-1) = -0.20000005 (computed).

verified.section: Part 2 L2.2
verified.claim: The restated L2.2 is still not an identifiability statement. An unordered transition set can be put back in order exactly, and the two worlds' retained state distributions differ. So 'a learner that treats transitions as an unordered set cannot tell the worlds apart' is false about the information in the data.
verified.evidence: Dynamics are deterministic, and observations are float32 casts of unique float64 states (datasets.py:336-337). Row t-1's next_obs equals row t's obs bit for bit, so a set rebuilds the trajectories. The gap left by a removed row then gives B+(s_{t+1} - A s_t - push), the draft's own ordered-trajectory argument (DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:103). The draft also reports that CUTOFF's retained states differ between worlds (line 274: about 0.2 less thrust per W- row, 0.4 on floor rows), so P_stall(D) ≠ P_nostall(D) even without ordering.
verified.fix: Restate as: the conditional law P(s', r | s, a) is identical on supp(D); the worlds differ only in the state marginal and in linkable gaps; and TD3+BC's critic and actor losses (td3_bc.py:174-245) use single tuples and never exploit either. Scope the claim to that algorithmic property, not to 'transition-set learners'.

check.reason: The wording is false as a statement about the information in the data. The consequences are already disclosed elsewhere, so this is a wording fix, not a validity problem. Each observation carries remaining time (datasets.py:338) and is an exact float32 cast of a float64 state (datasets.py:336-337). An unordered set of transitions therefore reorders trivially, through the time feature and bit-identical next_obs/obs links, and gaps then reveal thrust. That is the draft's own ordered-trajectory argument (line 103). The draft already discloses that the state marginals differ between worlds (lines 274-277, 560, 599). So L2.2's claim that 'a learner that treats transitions as an unordered set ... cannot tell the worlds apart' (line 102) should be scoped to per-tuple losses on an identical conditional law.
check.evidence: datasets.py:336-338 (obs[..., :13] == states.astype(float32); times = (100 - arange(101))/100). DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:102-103 and 274-277. Per-tuple losses in td3_bc.py at 174-245, as cited by the draft.

verified.section: Part 2 L2.1, L2.2 and the certainty table; step 0.4 KILL 1-2; Part 4.6
verified.claim: The 'exact to 1e-6, checked at every anchor' certainty for L2 cannot detect errors in rho. Because s' is identical for a0 and T(a0), the residual is independent of state, horizon, gamma, continuation and anchor reconstruction. The known-answer reproduction does not cover the new Q^pi settings either.
verified.evidence: Q(s,a) - Q(s,a') = r(s,a) - r(s,a') = -0.3(a0^2 - T^2) whenever s' is bit-identical (thrusterchain.py dynamics, lines 206-221). thrust(T(a0)) == T(a0) exactly (checked). A wrong anchor state, wrong t, wrong gamma or wrong continuation therefore cancels. The bit-identity check (KILL 2) tests only thrust() below the knee. rho = Qn(a0) - Qn(T) depends on the whole continuation and is never cross-checked. The 4.6 known answers come from old probes at FIXED_A0 = (-.5, -.25, 0, .25, .5) (rerun1/evaluation.py:17) at stall_slope 1.5. They do not cover stall_slope 3.0, W actions, anchors at t in {25, 50, 75} with a 100 - t horizon, or clipped continuations. Also, env.reset(options={'state'}) sets t = 0 and requires |s| ≤ 100 (thrusterchain.py reset), and the draft does not say how anchors at t > 0 are restored.
verified.fix: Downgrade the L2 certainty to 'identity checked; rho magnitudes rest on the Q^pi evaluator'. Add a second, independent Q^pi implementation (raw dynamics() loop vs environment) that must agree at every anchor. Add known-answer fixtures at stall_slope 3.0, with W actions and t > 0, including a horizon test (for example, a zero-continuation analytic case). Specify that anchors are restored by direct state and time assignment, not by reset.

check.reason: The finding's main sub-claims are refuted. (1) The old known-answer probes do cover anchors at t > 0 with 100 - t horizons and gamma 0.98. rerun1/evaluation.py builds anchors at times tile([0, 25, 50, 75]) by replaying random prefixes (lines 296-305), and the continuations sum horizons tile([100, 75, 50, 25]) (line 38). So 4.6's 1e-9 Q^pi reproduction tests the horizon, gamma and prefix-replay machinery. (2) Anchors are restored by replaying the prefix from reset (DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:92, 380), which gives the correct t, so the reset-sets-t=0 point is moot. (3) stall_slope 3.0 affects only the first-step thrust of a W action, which the identity checks. The identity reduces Q_stall(a0) to Q_stall at T in [-0.65, -0.2], which lies near or inside the old FIXED_A0 span [-0.5, 0.5]. (4) The gated items 1-3 of the L2 rule use only Q_stall and P_k fitted on supported slots, never Qn. Qn enters only item 5, where an error gives INCONCLUSIVE, the safe outcome. A wrong clip of the continuation either makes the worlds stall differently, which KILL 2 catches at supported slots, or still yields a valid non-stalling continuation. The certainty table describes the identity and the twin equality, and both claims are accurate.
check.evidence: rerun1/evaluation.py:36-38, 296-305 (times [0, 25, 50, 75], continuation horizons [100, 75, 50, 25], gamma 0.98 in protocol.json:306). DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:92, 110-115, 380, 386, 285-291. thrusterchain.py:435 (reset sets t=0, bypassed by prefix replay). T values at slope 3: -0.65, -0.5, -0.35, -0.2 for a0 = -0.85, -0.9, -0.95, -1 (computed).

verified.section: Part 2 L1.5 and Framing; Part 3.9 E2
verified.claim: 'Action shift, not state shift' is checked only at start states and recorder-prefix anchors. K2 and K3 are scored on free-rollout states that the learned policies themselves produce. In the stall world, entering W- weakens thrust and moves states away from the recorder's. E2 is also a subpopulation (covariate) shift from the 15% deep component, not 'not a state shift'.
verified.evidence: L1.5 (DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:81-83) gates on E2 starts and anchors only. K2 is the R_deep- rate on E2 free steps (line 444), and Δclip and J come from free rollouts (lines 414-418). In R_deep-, stall thrust is between -0.5 and -0.2 (T(-0.9) = -0.50000005, T(-1) = -0.20000005), against -0.8 to -0.5 on the recorder window at high load, so repeated entry changes the visited states. Deep-component episodes are 15% of training (Part 3.2); E2 draws only from that component, so P_E2(s) ≠ P_train(s) even though the supports overlap.
verified.fix: Apply the L1.5 kNN typicality statistic to each policy's visited E2 states, per arm and world (report it, or gate on it), and describe E2 as a subpopulation shift with overlapping support. In the framing, say that downstream state shift caused by the policy is part of the measured harm.

check.reason: The gap is real, but it is a reporting gap, not a validity defect. L1.5 (lines 81-83) gates only E2 start states and anchors. K2 and Δclip (lines 414-418, 444-448) come from free rollouts. In those rollouts, stall-world entry into R_deep- gives thrust of -0.5 to -0.2, weaker than any high-load window thrust the recorder delivered (-0.8 to -0.5). No visited-state typicality is reported. Downstream state shift caused by the policy is part of the harm that K3 is meant to measure, and Δclip is paired on identical starts, so attribution is not broken. 'So it is not a state shift' (line 167) is loose wording for a subpopulation draw, but L1.5 is the real check. The fix is to report kNN typicality on visited states per arm and world.
check.evidence: DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:81-83, 167, 414-418, 444. Thrust at slope 3: T(-0.9) = -0.50000005 and T(-1) = -0.20000005, against window thrust for a0 in [-0.9, -0.7], which is -0.7 to -0.8 to -0.5 (computed from thrusterchain.py:198).

verified.section: Part 2 L1.3
verified.claim: The convex-hull argument is imprecise. In an 18-D input, most fresh in-distribution queries already lie outside the hull of the training inputs, so 'the old Hole was interpolation' is unverified, and the hull is not the right notion of support. 'Strictly separates' is also wrong, because retained rows with a0 = -KNEE lie on the hyperplane.
verified.evidence: Scratch LP test (scratchpad/verify_wf/physics_ood/hull.py): with 20,000 Gaussian points in 18-D, only 4 of 20 fresh points lie inside the hull. Conversely, the hull contains inputs that are never supported: wave amplitude is drawn from U[0.1, 0.4], an annulus whose convex hull fills the disk. Retained inputs include a0 = -KNEE exactly (|a0| ≤ KNEE is retained), so the separation is weak, not strict.
verified.fix: Replace L1.3 with the marginal statement: every W- query has an a0 coordinate outside the range of retained a0 at every state, so the critic extrapolates along a0. Drop the claim that the old Hole was interpolation, or verify it with an LP hull test on the real retained inputs. Say 'weakly separates' (closed half-space).

check.reason: The claim that W- lies outside the hull is correct. 'The old Hole was interpolation' is unverified in the convex-hull sense and probably false: in 18-D, typical in-distribution queries lie outside the hull of the training points. This is rhetorical framing, not a gate, so the severity is low. 'Strictly separates' is pedantically imprecise but harmless. The expected number of retained rows at exactly float32 -KNEE is about 0.01, and W- is an open half-space, so the sets are disjoint either way.
check.evidence: My own LP test (scratchpad/verify_wf/physics_skeptic/chk.py): 5,000 Gaussian points in 18-D, and 0 of 20 fresh draws lie inside their convex hull. This is consistent with the other reviewer's 4/20 at 20k points. DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:72.

verified.section: Part 2 L1.4
verified.claim: The L1.4 interval [1.9, 3.1] is about 30 standard errors wide, so it cannot catch the most plausible control bug, and it pools mid and deep load, so it never checks the E2-relevant deep-load labels.
verified.evidence: Expected band count ≈ 44,160 high-load rows × 0.2484 ≈ 10,970, an iid relative SD of 0.8% (scratch mc.py). If RANDOM is implemented without load stratification (uniform retention 1 - 0.369), the density is 4.91 × 0.631 = 3.098, which is inside [1.9, 3.1]. The test fails only if RANDOM keeps none or all of the W rows. Deep-load band rows are about 1,480 of the 10,970 and are not checked separately.
verified.fix: Use an episode-cluster-bootstrap 99.9% interval, or ±10% around 2.48, and report it separately for mid and deep load bands. Note that 4.5's per-stratum count check is what actually catches unstratified removal.

check.reason: The arithmetic checks out. Full band density = 4.91. Stratified retention gives 4.91 x 0.506 = 2.484. Unstratified retention (0.631) gives 3.098, inside [1.9, 3.1]. The iid relative SD is about 0.95% (about 10,971 retained band rows), so the interval's half-width is about 25 SDs. A deep-stratum fault that kept zero deep band labels gives a pooled 2.147, which also passes. The severity is low for two reasons. 4.5's gated per-stratum count equality (line 270, KILL 4 at line 388) catches unstratified removal. A deep-stratum selection bug that keeps counts equal would most likely surface as a V0(b) INCONCLUSIVE rather than a wrong conclusion. Tightening the interval and reporting it by mid/deep band is still cheap and worthwhile.

packed.verdict: The draft is much better on paper than the panel plan. Units are now declared, outcomes are split into consistent and mixed failures, recovery has a denominator guard, and AUROC is computed within each anchor. But the kill-rule logic still has three defects that could decide the outcome. (1) Step 0.3's new reach model fits a quadratic through a0 = -0.9 and -1. The old critics had slope-1.5 labels at those points. In the same step, G0.5 lets the study proceed only if those critics represent the fold, so the two gates work against each other. My reconstruction from saved per-probe Q1 gives a probe forecast of 0.000 in all nine cells once the critics hold about 40% of the fold, while G0.5 needs about 87%. So step 0.3 can pass only if G0.5's critics are wrong. (2) The Stage 2 robustness screens are J thresholds of the same size as the noise between branches from one fork, and nothing makes them specific to the region. The prior study's BCA-vs-native gap from the same forks was +3.6 ± 3.55 (discounted, strong current), including full-data cells where nothing was withheld. verified.section: Part 5, step 0.3 (reach model vs G0.5), DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md lines 347-370
verified.claim: Step 0.3's reach forecast and the G0.5 fold test, run in the same step, work against each other. The forecast fits a six-point quadratic that includes a0 = -0.9 and -1. The old critics had slope-1.5 labels at those points, so any critic that represents the fold (which G0.5 requires) bends the fit at the knee and forces the reach KILL. The forecast measures labelled critics, not the unlabelled CUTOFF extrapolation it is meant to predict.
verified.evidence: Scratch script verify_wf/killrule_stats/fold.py and fold2.py. They take each saved strong-current high-load probe's Q1 quadratic on [-0.5, 0.5] (reproduces step 0.1: mix15/C probe minimum 0.562, maximum 0.781). They then replace the values at -0.9 and -1 with a fraction f of the exact slope-1.5 identity, Q(T(a)) - 0.3(a^2 - T^2), fit the step 0.3 six-point quadratic, and apply pi0 = (m + 2λ'b)/(1 - 4λ'c) with m = -0.7263 and λ' = saved λ × 0.751. Minimum probe forecast over the 9 cells: f = 0 gives 0.562; f = 0.2 gives 0.375; f = 0.3 gives 0.188; f >= 0.4 gives 0.000 in every cell, against the KILL bar of 0.35. The median fold error F at f = 0.2 is 2.55, while G0.5 proceeds cleanly only with median F <= 0.5, which corresponds to f of about 0.87. The fitted curvature c moves from about -0.7 (no fold) to about -22 to -31 (full fold). Caveat: G0.5 is governed on the ordinary bank and the forecast on strong-current rows, so a pass on both requires critics that hold the fold at ordinary states but miss it at strong-current states. Those strong-current states are outside the critics' training data, so such a pass would itself be a failure of the critics there.
verified.fix: Fit the forecast only on supported slots at or inside the knee, {-0.5, -0.6, -0.7, -KNEE}, extrapolating linearly or quadratically past -KNEE. That matches what an unlabelled CUTOFF critic sees. Alternatively, use only the Q1 values inside the knee and state the extrapolation rule. Set this before A2. Report the six-point version descriptively only.

packed.verdict: Most of the code facts in Part 4 check out: line numbers, cadence, gamma handling, the float32 predicate, the twin-world construction and the warmup timings. The certification layer still has two real gaps and several wrong numbers. First, the arithmetic for the RANDOM control is wrong. Count-matched removal within small strata (mean 6.3 rows) removes withheld rows more often than chance. RANDOM therefore keeps about 48% of withheld labels, not 57%. The L1.4 density is about 2.08, not 2.48, and the RANDOM BC anchor is about -0.775, not -0.784. The prior study's saved geometry.json shows the same shortfall (6,184 of 9,692 kept, against about 7,270 by the simple formula). As a result, the "test that can fail" in L1.4 is centered on the wrong value, and it passes an unstratified RANDOM about half the time. Second, section 4.3b ties its in-worker proof to upstream make_train_step. The reused pipeline trains through candidate.make_microsteps and re-binds the replay at every fork. Calibration, probe and normalization arrays also reach the learner but are not covered. Smaller problems: (1) the calibration split does not match the prior study's convention, and giving each arm its own calibration rows departs from the prior's common calibration without saying so; (2) the reset-mixture draw order does not match draw_starts; (3) evaluation throughput is overstated by about 1.9x; (4) there is no BC-only harness; (5) a few citations and test specifications are imprecise. None of this invalidates the design, but L1.4, the Part 3 expected values, 4.3b and the calibration plan must be corrected before A1 can certify implementation.

verified.section: Part 3 item 7; L1.4; Step 0.1 arithmetic; Part 6.1/6.3; Part 9
verified.claim: RANDOM's expected label retention, the L1.4 expected density and the RANDOM BC anchor are all wrong. They assume independent retention, but count-matching within small strata removes withheld rows preferentially. As a result, L1.4 cannot detect an unstratified RANDOM.
verified.evidence: Monte Carlo of the stated rule, matching episode x ten-step bin x load band (scratchpad verify_wf/impl_cert/mc2.py and mc.py, 300 replicate datasets). Mean stratum size is 6.3 rows, and 58% of rows sit in strata of fewer than 10. Results: RANDOM keeps 48.1% of withheld labels (draft: 57%); high-load withheld retention is 42.4% (simple formula: 50.6%); the RANDOM high-load anchor is -0.775 (draft: -0.784); the L1.4 density is 2.083 +/- 0.015, 99.9% range [2.043, 2.123] (draft expects 2.48). An unstratified RANDOM gives 3.097 +/- 0.023, range [3.033, 3.167], so it passes the bar [1.9, 3.1] about 56% of the time. The prior study's saved data show the same effect: conditional_ood_gate_central_quartile_v1/run/geometry.json has random_retained_hole_rows 6184 of 9692 (63.8%), against 75% from the simple formula. The prior control_masks (geometry.py:112-128) used the same mechanism. The 'about 5x' label density is really about 4.2x, and the BC-anchor gap is 0.049, not 0.058.
verified.fix: Recompute every RANDOM expected value by simulating the exact stratified rule, and seal those values under A1. Re-center L1.4 on the simulated value with a bar of about +/-6 SD (for example [1.98, 2.18]). Add a synthetic test that requires an unstratified RANDOM, and a RANDOM that ignores load band, to fail L1.4. Correct Part 3.7, Step 0.1, Part 6 and Part 9.

check.reason: The arithmetic error is real. RANDOM picks `count` rows uniformly from all n rows in a stratum, withheld rows included (prior geometry.py:112-128 uses rng.choice(rows, count) over every row). So the expected withheld-row retention is (n-1)/n x (1-p), not (1-p). Strata are episode x ten-step bin x load band, so n <= 10. That puts high-load W retention at <= 0.9 x 0.506 = 0.455, below the draft's implied 0.506. The draft's 57% (Part 3.7, Part 6.1), its 2.48 density (L1.4, Step 0.1), the 'about 5x' and the -0.784 anchor therefore all overstate RANDOM's labels. Saved evidence confirms the mechanism: the prior gate kept 6184 of 9692 hole rows = 63.8%, against 75% from the simple formula, which implies n_eff of about 6.8. The detection half of the claim is weaker. An unstratified RANDOM would indeed sit at about 3.10, at the edge of the [1.9, 3.1] bar. But Part 4.5 (line 270, 'RANDOM's per-stratum counts equal CUTOFF's') and the 4.3b alignment fixture on wrong strata already catch a mis-stratified RANDOM, so L1.4 is not the only guard. The true value of about 2.08 still lies inside [1.9, 3.1], so Step 0.4 kill item 7 will not fire spuriously. What remains is wrong sealed expected values and an overstated control strength. I downgraded it from high to medium.

critic.verdict: The draft is not ready for A1 as written. It could be ready for the user to consider A1 once the must-fix items below are made. A1 seals the protocol, every kill rule for steps 0.3 to Stage 2, and the expected values that the count checks test against. So every gate-defining fix has to land before A1, not after it. Two defects can decide the outcome on their own. (1) The step 0.3 reach forecast fits through a0 = -0.9 and -1, where the old critics had labels. Any critic that holds 40% or more of the fold then forces the KILL (0.000 in all 9 cells), while G0.5 in the same step requires the critics to hold the fold. (2) The Stage 2 'promising' screens are J thresholds about the size of between-branch noise, with no requirement that the gain is specific to the withheld region. The prior BCA-minus-native gaps were +3.6 ± 3.55, including +4.28/+1.20/+4.52 in full-data cells where nothing was withheld. Close behind those: Stage 2 has no check that the native replicate reproduces the damage and no outcome labels. The label system is not exhaustive across 0.3, 0.4 and Stage 2: the G0.5 STOP contradicts Part 8 item 2. K1 has no absolute over-valuation floor and V0(b) is one-sided. K3c tests a different policy than L3c describes. RANDOM's sealed expected values are wrong: it keeps about 48% of W labels, not 57%, the density is about 2.08, not 2.48, and the anchor is about -0.775, not -0.784. 4.3b targets a function the reused pipeline never calls. The calibration split contradicts itself. The physics, the predicate, the stall identity, the twin construction and most of the arithmetic all reproduce. The remaining problems are in the rule logic, the control's expected values, and how certification connects to the actual training path. All of them can be fixed on paper without new data.

must_fix.issue: The local quadratic is fit through all six points, including a0 = -0.9 and -1. All nine frozen critics were trained on uniform slope-1.5 data with labels at those points (line 349 uses the slope-1.5 identity for these very critics). So the forecast measures labelled critics, not the unlabelled CUTOFF extrapolation it claims to predict. Reconstruction from saved per-probe Q1 (verify_wf/killrule_stats/fold2.py, re-run by the skeptic): minimum probe forecast 0.562 at f=0, 0.375 at f=0.2, 0.188 at f=0.3, and 0.000 in every cell for f >= 0.4, against the 0.35 KILL bar. G0.5 proceeds cleanly only at median F <= 0.5, roughly f ≈ 0.87. The two gates in the same step therefore work against each other.

critic.can_be_certain:
Once the must-fix items are made, these parts can honestly be called certain, meaning exact by construction and checked row by row or bit for bit:
(1) The withheld-region predicate: |float64(float32 a0)| > KNEE, with KNEE = 0.800000011920929. Three implementations agree, and every CUTOFF data stream has exactly 0 W rows, provided 4.3b is re-targeted to the arrays that candidate.make_microsteps actually binds.
(2) Separation along a0: every W- query lies outside the range of retained a0 at every state. This is a fact about the a0 coordinate, not a convex-hull claim.
(3) Load g does not depend on actions, so the twin worlds' requested actions, loads and masks are byte-identical.
(4) Thrust is bit-identical in both worlds for |a_k| <= KNEE, so the conditional transition law P(s', r | s, a) is identical on the retained support. Non-identifiability is certain only as a property of per-tuple learners such as TD3+BC, not as a claim about the information in the data.
(5) The stall identity Q_stall(s, a) = Q_stall(s, a0 <- T(a0)) - 0.3(a0^2 - T^2) is an exact algebraic fact of the simulator, checkable to float precision.
(6) The recorder's closed-form density, the exact P(g >= 0.4) = 0.575, and count reconciliation against bounds that are re-derived by simulation and sealed.
Two things are exact computations but depend on assumptions, so they should not be presented as unconditional certainties: the true value gap rho at an anchor is exact given a stated continuation policy and the Q^pi evaluator, but its size depends on that continuation, which in step 0.4 is old actors outside their training distribution; RANDOM's expected label retention is exact only once simulated under the exact stratified rule.
Everything else can only be measured, and each can fail as a valid result: the predictor-based residual rho_hat; L1.5 state typicality; whether the CUTOFF critic over-values the region (K1); whether the actor goes there (K2, R0); whether going there costs return (K3); the step 0.3 reach forecasts; whether RANDOM's critic represents the knee (V0(b), G0.5); BCA's detection AUROC; and every Stage 2 J or repair screen. L3 is a gate, not a guarantee. The 3-of-3 seed rules have unstated and probably low power, so a FAIL-mixed is not evidence of absence.
